chunks: Your intercourse with your wives is permitted on the night of fasting. They are your garment and you are their garment. God knew that you were deceiving yourselves, so He turned to you in mercy and pardoned you. So now, have intercourse with them and seek what God has ordained for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread of night, then complete the fast until nightfall; and do not have intercourse with them while you are in consecration in the mosques. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus God makes His signs clear to people so that they may become pious.

key_terms.الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْ: The white thread and black thread (referring to dawn light)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and rules for marital intimacy during Ramadan fasting?
ai.summary: This verse (2:187) clarifies the permissibility of marital intimacy during Ramadan nights, using the metaphor of spouses as 'garments' for one another to signify mutual protection, comfort, and modesty. It establishes the precise start and end times for the fast and prohibits intercourse during I'tikaf, defining these boundaries as divine limits (hudud) to cultivate God-consciousness (taqwa).
